messages:
alex_k: Heads-up — planning a maintenance window on rack r12 (us-west2-b). Purpose: replace flaky ephemeral NVMe nodes + apply new GPU driver (440.64 -> 450.12). Rolling drains, 5 nodes at a time, estimated start Tue 2026-04-06 02:00 UTC, ~2h total for the rack. Expect brief node-level capacity dips; we'll keep pool-level throughput but < 10% reduction during hot-swap.

maria_s: Which pools will be affected? Any Dedicated customers on that rack?

alex_k: Affected pools: `gpu-pool-usw2-hosted` (primary) and `dedicated-reserved-usw2-cohort-c` (2 nodes pinned). We'll avoid draining nodes with pinned VMs unless we get approvals. Dedicated customers: outreach list sent to SEs, short notice only for non-pinned.

samir_r: Important: long-running batch jobs may get evicted — we should set `evictionGracePeriod` to 10m and force drain only after that. Also want to ensure checkpointing jobs are bumped to next node.

diane_l: +1. Plan to annotate pods with `redwood/maintenance-safe=true` for critical tasks so scheduler can skip them. Also recommend prefix cache warmup before traffic switches.

leo_ops: Runbook draft and command snippets below. I'll kick off a canary on the first node and monitor GPU temp + NVMe SMART. If canary looks good, continue cohort.

leo_ops: ```
# cordon + drain with graceful period
kubectl cordon node-r12-03
kubectl drain node-r12-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=600 --force

# quick prewarm of prefix cache after restart
for i in {1..20}; do curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $WARMUP_KEY" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"prefix warmup"}' >/dev/null; done
```

maria_s: How are we routing latency-sensitive routes during drain? Can we policy-route to eu-west1 for small percent of traffic?

alex_k: Yes — we'll set routing policy: `latency_sensitive -> eu-west1` fallback at 5% traffic during the window, automatic fallback to cheaper pool if eu-west is saturated. This will add cross-region egress cost (~$0.02/token estimate on heavy tails) but only for canary traffic.

samir_r: Any kv/prefix-cache cold-start risk? If yes, we should plan a short burst of prewarming after each node rejoin. Also note that quantized kernels may need warm compile on first run (adds ~150ms).

diane_l: We'll run post-restart smoke tests: perf-checker job (latency p50/p95), and a correctness eval against 10 golden prompts. If regressions > threshold, auto-rollback to old driver and reprovision node.

ops-bot: scheduled maintenance created: https://infra.redwood/maint/1742109876 — window: 2026-04-06 02:00–04:00 UTC — owner: leo_ops

oncall-bot: Reminder set: 30m pre-window and 5m pre-window pings to #eng-oncall and SE on duty. Pager suppression: false.

maria_s: Customer comms: SEs to send targeted DMs to 3 Dedicated customers on the pinned list. I'll coordinate the wording.

alex_k: Quick capacity note: backfill with spot nodes during drain will temporarily increase cost by ~3.2% for the day. If budget-sensitivity is high we can spread smaller drains across two nights to reduce backfill spikes but increases total maintenance duration.

samir_r: Suggest we avoid evicting GPU workloads during US peak (14:00–22:00 PST). Our chosen window is OK.

diane_l: All good from platform side. Please add a step in the runbook to verify NVMe SMART health post-replace: `nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0n1`. If anything anomalous, mark node for deeper triage.

leo_ops: Will add checks + automated rollback. I'll run canary at 02:00 UTC, post results in this thread. If no objections, I'll flip the scheduled job to `confirmed`. :white_check_mark:

maria_s: Confirmed. SE outreach approved. No objections from leadership. Proceed. :thumbsup:

alex_k: Thanks — coordinating with CS and oncall. Will post canary result ~02:20 UTC.
